introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklets are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One Hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

Figure 1 shows how three resistors, three batteries with internal resistances and ammeters are connected in a network.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 1 : network between junctions M and N with three parallel branches. Left branch: 3 ohm resistor, 9 V battery with 1 ohm internal resistance and ammeter B. Middle branch: ammeter A, 4 ohm resistor and 3 V battery with 2 ohm internal resistance. Right branch: 5 ohm resistor, 11 V battery with 3 ohm internal resistance and ammeter C.

incertitudes: Question 3 : polarités lues sur la figure. Dans chacune des trois branches la plaque longue (positive) de la pile est du côté de M, donc les trois piles tendent à envoyer le courant de N vers M. Les ampèremètres sont supposés idéaux (résistance nulle) et les résistances internes de 1, 2 et 3 ohms sont en série avec la résistance de leur branche. Si une polarité était lue à l'envers, les résultats changeraient : lecture du schéma à vérifier.

Question 3 : le sujet imprime « Calculate the; » suivi de i), ii), iii) sans lettre : une seule question de numéro 1 avec (i) à (iii) dans le texte. Seul le total « (8 marks) » est imprimé. Le courant dans A circule de M vers N (il charge la pile de 3 V), l'ampèremètre indique sa valeur absolue.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the;

(i) readings of the meters A, B and C.

(ii) potential difference between M and N.

(iii) power dissipated as heat in the $5\ \Omega$ resistor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading the circuit.** Between M and N there are three branches in parallel. In each branch the cell has its longer (positive) plate towards M, so each cell tends to push current from N to M. The ammeters are ideal. Total resistance of each branch (resistor + internal resistance):

| Branch | e.m.f. | Resistance |
|---|---|---|
| left (meter B) | $9\ \mathrm{V}$ | $3 + 1 = 4\ \Omega$ |
| middle (meter A) | $3\ \mathrm{V}$ | $4 + 2 = 6\ \Omega$ |
| right (meter C) | $11\ \mathrm{V}$ | $5 + 3 = 8\ \Omega$ |

**(ii) Potential difference between M and N.** Let $V$ be the p.d. of M above N. For a branch with e.m.f. $E$ and resistance $R$, the current towards M is $I = \dfrac{E - V}{R}$ (a negative value means the current flows from M to N). Kirchhoff's current law at M: the three currents arriving at M add up to zero (M is joined to nothing else):

$$\frac{9-V}{4} + \frac{3-V}{6} + \frac{11-V}{8} = 0.$$

Multiply by $24$: $6(9-V) + 4(3-V) + 3(11-V) = 0 \Rightarrow 54 + 12 + 33 = 13V \Rightarrow V = \dfrac{99}{13}$.

$$V_{MN} = 7.62\ \mathrm{V}\ (\text{M is positive with respect to N}).$$

**(i) Readings of the meters.**

- Meter B (left branch): $I_B = \dfrac{9 - 7.615}{4} = 0.346\ \mathrm{A}$, towards M.
- Meter C (right branch): $I_C = \dfrac{11 - 7.615}{8} = 0.423\ \mathrm{A}$, towards M.
- Meter A (middle branch): $I_A = \dfrac{3 - 7.615}{6} = -0.769\ \mathrm{A}$: the current flows from M to N through the middle branch (it charges the $3\ \mathrm{V}$ cell), of magnitude $0.769\ \mathrm{A}$.

Check at the junction: $0.346 + 0.423 = 0.769\ \mathrm{A}$ leaves M through the middle branch. Check with a loop (left and middle branches): $9 - 3 = 4(0.346) + 6(0.769) = 1.385 + 4.615 = 6.00\ \mathrm{V}$. Correct.

**Readings: A $= 0.769\ \mathrm{A}$, B $= 0.346\ \mathrm{A}$, C $= 0.423\ \mathrm{A}$.**

**(iii) Power dissipated as heat in the $5\ \Omega$ resistor.** The current in it is $I_C = 0.423\ \mathrm{A}$:
$$P = I_C^{2}R = (0.423)^{2}\times5 = 0.895\ \mathrm{W}.$$

**Power $\approx 0.90\ \mathrm{W}$.**
